# onpager_schedule_handover (Resource)

Manage one schedule's handover notification settings and selected on-call catalog bindings.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "onpager_schedule_handover" "example" {
  team_id            = "11111111-1111-4111-8111-111111111111"
  schedule_id        = "22222222-2222-4222-8222-222222222222"
  enabled            = false
  oncall_channel_ids = []
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `enabled` (Boolean) Whether future observed on-call changes are broadcast. Required without a default; null is invalid. true requires at least one oncall_channel_ids entry. false retains explicitly selected channels until updated; destroy always clears them. Ordinary changes require an active owner; canonical false plus [] cleanup also works with an inactive owner or disabled schedule.
- `oncall_channel_ids` (Set of String) Complete set of 0–100 distinct nonzero canonical lowercase binding UUIDs from the owning team's on-call channel catalog. These are catalog binding IDs, not delivery-channel UUIDs. Required without a default; null is invalid and explicit [] clears selections. enabled=true requires a nonempty set. The provider performs no discovery, target lookup, preview or delivery.
- `schedule_id` (String) Immutable schedule UUID belonging to team_id, required without a default. Changing it replaces this settings slot. Must be a nonzero canonical lowercase UUID.
- `team_id` (String) Immutable owning team UUID, required without a default. Changing it replaces this settings slot. Must be a nonzero canonical lowercase UUID.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Stable scoped identity `team_id/schedule_id`, also used for import.
- `revision` (Number) Independent handover-settings revision sent in the PUT body for compare-and-swap, without If-Match. Unwritten settings have revision 0; stored settings have positive revisions. Schedule settings/rotation revisions are never used. Stale writes return HTTP 409 and require a fresh plan.

## Import

Import using `team_id/schedule_id`, with both parts as nonzero canonical
lowercase UUIDs. An unwritten slot (`revision: 0`) has no managed settings to
import.

Use an `import` block:

```terraform
import {
  to = onpager_schedule_handover.example
  id = "11111111-1111-4111-8111-111111111111/22222222-2222-4222-8222-222222222222"
}
```

Or use the CLI:

```shell
terraform import onpager_schedule_handover.example 11111111-1111-4111-8111-111111111111/22222222-2222-4222-8222-222222222222
```

## Lifecycle

Manage each schedule's handover settings slot once. Changing the immutable team
or schedule UUID replaces the resource. Both `enabled` and the complete
`oncall_channel_ids` set are required. Null is invalid; an explicit empty set
clears the selected channels. Enabling requires at least one explicit binding
UUID from the owning team's on-call channel catalog. A catalog binding UUID
differs from a delivery channel UUID.

Create reads the exact slot, then sends PUT with its observed body `revision`.
Updates and destroy use the saved handover revision, independently of schedule
settings, rotations and overrides. `If-Match` is not sent. Stale writes return
HTTP 409 and require a new plan. A confirmed successful write with a malformed
receipt retains the scoped identity and available revision for refresh.

Destroy writes `enabled: false` and `oncall_channel_ids: []`, retaining settings
and history. This cleanup works under an inactive team or disabled schedule;
ordinary changes retain the API's active-owner requirements. Failure retains
state. A successful exact read with revision zero confirms an unwritten slot and
removes state. HTTP errors, including 404, and malformed responses retain it.
Disabled stored settings with a positive revision remain managed.

Saving or enabling starts a quiet baseline without an immediate announcement.
Future observed on-call changes can notify the selected channels. Rotations,
overrides and catalog bindings are managed separately.

## Permissions

Requires owning-team grants `schedules.read` and `schedules.update`, including
for service accounts. Read and update authority are independent.
